newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Weak gasoline could break support for Brent.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Weak gasoline could break support for Brent.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 29 -------------
* Brent needs to hold above trendline support that has been leading it higher over the past six days to avoid a crash, but weakness in NYMEX gasoline could push it over the edge.
* NYMEX gasoline is so overbought at the moment a close below $18.47 tonight on the prompt Brent contract would be disastrous.

IPE Brent needs to hold above trendline support that has been leading the market higher over the past six days to avoid a crash, but some analyst see weakness in overbought NYMEX gasoline pushing it over the edge.
Gas oil must break $168 convincingly to go higher.
Tom James, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore, said the Brent market was "just hanging on to support".

"Brent (September futures) only just managed to close above key trendline support last night, closing at $18.41 with support at $18.40 representing a support trendline which has been leading the market higher over the past six days and that has been tested six times so far," James said.
He said that with NYMEX gasoline so overbought at the moment a close below $18.47 tonight on the prompt contract will be disastrous.
"This is the only technical support around at the moment for this contract and if this is combined with a breakdown in NYMEX gasoline then lookout $18 and below," he explained.

To the upside analysts said the market has some stiff resistance levels to breakdown with $18.70 on the September chart providing initial daily high-low resistance then Fibonacci resistance at $18.80 and trendline resistance at $19.
Key trendline support is at $18.47 today with the previously congested $18.11 region offering limited support underneath this.

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives Limited said in her daily report, "API numbers due later today are suggesting unfriendly gasoline data which may, in the short term put the brakes on technical strength".

However, despite the underlying bearishness for the September chart, technical support appears intact on the daily spot month continuation chart with price action holding well above trendline support that rises up through the key lows from the June 11 trough at $17.32.
Analyst believe that while the prices are on the right side of this line the seven week uptrend looks ongoing.

They said the upper and lower trend lines on the spot month continuation chart for Brent, starting with the June 11 low of $17.32 and high $17.90 and passing through the July 15 low of $17.80 and the July 17 high of $18.79 respectively, are still seen capping and underpinning the market though this expanding wedge pattern is usually read as a bearish signal.
Gas oil too remains well above trendline support on the daily spot month continuation chart stemming from the July 15 low of $160 through $162-$163.25 and coming in today at around $165.75.
Analysts said last Thursday's perfect Doji formation on the spot chart, where the market opened and closed at the same level, proved to be supportive rather than a downside flag.

Prices made good headway either side of the weekend peaking at $167.75 on Friday on the back of stronger crude and briefly breaking resistance at $168 a double top from July 3 and July 17 on Monday, but analysts said the market needed to break this level more convincingly to go any higher.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
